# The Commerce deck

**What it rewards:** Routes, partnerships, goods and deliberate spending. **Directions inside it:** established domestic partners; overseas posts; manufactured and export goods; reserves versus purchased capability.

*Generated by `scripts/deckDocs.mjs` from `data/decks/*.json` and the describers' own words. A card is **built** when the game can deal it — a row carrying a deferred sentence and no effects is in the data and the Compendium and in no pool. **Edit this file freely: your edits are the spec.** The generator is run on request only and overwrites everything here, annotations included.*

| Card | Rarity | Status | The card | What the game does, or why not |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Salt Tithes** | common | built | Gain +3 gold per distinct accessible improved luxury you produce. Worked luxury tiles gain +1 food. | +3 gold per unique luxury · +1 food on every hex carrying a luxury resource |
| **The Guild Halls** | common | built | A city gains +1 production per distinct luxury type it works. Worked camps and plantations gain +1 food. | +1 production in every city per unique luxury there · +1 food on every hex with a Camp or Plantation |
| **The Merchant Shrines** | common | built | Your capital gains +2 faith. Cities working an improved luxury gain +2 faith, once per city. | +2 faith in your capital · +2 faith in every city holding an improved luxury resource |
| **Travellers' Letters** | common | deferred | Your capital gains +2 science and +2 culture, plus +1 of each per foreign empire met, at most +4 additional science and culture. | Half built, and so held whole. Nothing in this game counts the empires you have met, so the letters have nobody to be addressed to. |
| **Letters of Introduction** | common | deferred | First contact with each foreign empire grants you 100 gold and that empire 15 gold. Contact recorded before activation cannot pay retrospectively. Discoveries yield 15 gold. | Held whole. The world does not announce a first meeting, and no law of yours can put coin in another realm's treasury. |
| **The Pathfinders' Company** | uncommon | built | Scouts gain +1 sight and +1 movement. | scouts: +1 sight · scouts: +1 movement |
| **The Lighthouse Keepers** | common | built | Ships gain +1 sight. Lighthouses cost 25% less production; worked fishing boats gain +1 food. | ships: +1 sight · +25% production toward Lighthouses · +1 food on every hex with a Fishing Boat |
| **The Assayer's Rule** | uncommon | built | +2 gold on resource tiles that supply gold | +2 gold on every hex carrying a resource that yields gold |
| **Private Patronage** | rare | deferred | Gold purchases of ordinary buildings cost 20% less. Producing those buildings normally takes 20% more production. Empire buildings and wonders are unaffected. | Held whole. The realm's single great houses can be named now, and a marvel always could — but neither can be named by its absence, and this card is a discount on every building that is neither, so a discount written here would reach the great houses the card says it must not. |
